articles.title: Poland foils attempted 'provocation' on Russian border, PM Tusk says
articles.description: Prime Minister Donald Tusk said Tuesday that Poland prevented an attempted "provocation" on its border with the Russian exclave of Kaliningrad overnight. He gave few details but said Polish security forces prevented any incident from happening.

articles.title: US Supreme court rejects Trump request to set aside 20,000 California ballots
articles.description: The US Supreme Court rejected the Trump administration’s push to force California to set aside 20,000 ballots from people the federal government claims are noncitizens, a decision that came hours before the final day of voting in the pivotal midterm elections. FRANCE 24's correspondent Wassim Cornet reports.

articles.title: What could happen if Donald Trump loses US midterm elections?
articles.description: Americans head to the polls on Tuesday in pivotal midterm elections, with Democrats hoping to seize control of Congress and impose the first significant checks on Donald Trump's second term in the White House. But what could happen in the United States if Republicans lose control of Congress? FRANCE 24's International Affairs Editor Philip Turle has more.

articles.description: As the US approaches the midterms, the contest is emerging as a referendum on Donald Trump, the resilience of American democratic institutions and the ability of a divided Democratic Party to transform widespread public dissatisfaction into a coherent political alternative. articles.description: Senegal's powerful opposition party Pastef led by former presidential candidate Ousmane Sonko on Tuesday rejected a revised version of the country's budget, leaving the west African nation's new bailout programme with the International Monetary Fund hanging in the balance.

articles.title: Uganda withdraws its troops from Somalia as fight against rebels persists
articles.description: Kampala announced on Monday it had begun pulling its troops out of Somalia. Uganda was the first country to send deployments to help Mogadishu when the African Union set up an international military mission in 2007 to battle al-Shabab extremist rebels. But what is prompting Kampala to withdraw its troops now, as the battle against the militants continues? FRANCE 24’s Georga Calvin Smith is joined by Horn of Africa geopolitical analyst Anwar Abdifatah Bashir.

articles.title: South Africans demand security and basic services as they vote in local elections
articles.description: High crime rates and a lack of basic services are causing concern among many of South Africa’s 29 million registered voters. Water shortages and unreliable electricity supplies have also become symbols of municipal failures, angering voters and eroding support for the ruling African National Congress. The municipal elections on November 4 will offer a glimpse into whether these frustrations are shifting political loyalties.

articles.title: "Des fois, j'ai des trous de mémoire" : au premier jour de leur procès, l'état de santé des parents de la "martyre de l'A10" au cœur des débats
articles.description: Ahmed Touloub, 74 ans, et Halima El Bakhti, 72 ans, sont jugés par la cour d'assises du Loir-et-Cher, près de quarante ans après que la petite Inass a été retrouvée morte et mutilée. Le père devra faire l'objet d'une expertise psychiatrique complémentaire à la demande de la défense.

articles.title: Midterms: Trump uses final appeal to talk about troubled Reflecting Pool
articles.description: In his final major speech before midterm elections in which polls but the Democrats well ahead of the Republican Party, Donald Trump on Monday spent more than 20 minutes discussing pipes, joints and caulking as he touted his troubled renovations to the Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool in Washington. To many critics, the renovations have become a symbol of government incompetence and misplaced priorities after delays caused by peeling paint and algae growth ‌that turned the pool’s waters green.
